leads.summary: Inherited namespace marker plus unrelated caller ID can bypass unshare on a root runner
leads.consequence: If a root test process inherits OMARCHY_WINDOWS_BOUNDARY_NAMESPACE=1 and any nonempty OMARCHY_WINDOWS_BOUNDARY_CALLER_MOUNT_NS different from its current mount namespace, the script does not call unshare. It accepts the unequal ID and mounts tmpfs over /run, /var and /home in the runner's actual namespace. The new runtime probes always supply equal or absent caller IDs, so do not test this combination. Requires inherited/contaminated environment; ordinary unset variables are handled by the intended reexec.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N4, reproduced); needs both vars preset, plain sudo resets env; not published

leads.summary: A failed second readlink is treated as proof that the mount namespace changed
leads.consequence: If recording the caller succeeds but readlink /proc/self/ns/mnt fails on reentry, the command substitution becomes empty and its failure is discarded inside [[ ... != ... ]]; empty differs from the nonempty caller ID. A root run then reaches the real /run mount instead of failing closed. The initial `export VAR=$(readlink ...)` also masks the first readlink status, though its empty output is rejected by the later nonempty check. This is an error-path finding, not a claim that /proc normally fails.
leads.triage: behavioural: neutral follow-up to Opus; confirmed fail-open by sandbox run, harm needs double fault

leads.summary: The new regression test accepts an early mount before unshare
leads.consequence: An inserted `mount -t tmpfs early-mount /run` immediately after the marker `if` and before `exec unshare` is later than guard_line, so the static check passes. Both dynamic probes set the marker to 1, bypass that branch and pass as well. On a normal marker-unset root invocation the new mount would execute in the caller's namespace before isolation. A sandboxed, copied-file mutant returned four ok lines and exit 0; no host mounts were made. The scan also misses an earlier `mount -o` or `command mount` when a later bare mount still matches, and is limited to the hard-coded MOUNTING_TESTS.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1, reproduced); corroboration

leads.summary: Current quattro conflicts on the namespace-unavailable line, and keeping pass hides skips
leads.consequence: A three-way merge against quattro tip 8b4eae66 conflicts between PR's `pass ... skipping ...` and base's `skip ... skipping ...`. Current base-test.sh has a skip helper and current test/shell reports # SKIP lines; resolving this hunk to pass would make unavailable mount-namespace coverage appear to have passed. Choose skip with accurate new reason when rebasing. Open #9783 and #10962 also have this exact pass/skip merge-file conflict; it is the same base change, not additional independent conflicts.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (merge state); corroboration

leads.summary: The claimed every-mounting-test fail-closed check is not applied to the compose test
leads.consequence: Both actual mounting shell tests are listed, but only windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh gets the runtime same/unset namespace-ID tests. windows-vm-compose-test.sh has a marker gate and real mount and umount commands, yet no recorded caller mount namespace or reentry comparison. When its marker is inherited as 1 it proceeds without unsharing, including under a root runner. The docs assertion that the new test holds both halves in place for every mounting test overstates coverage. No compose runtime root execution was attempted.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); coordinator verified quattro files

leads.summary: A missing grep match silently aborts the new test before its fail diagnostic
leads.consequence: With set -euo pipefail, a grep no-match makes `guard_line=$(grep ... | head -1 | cut ...)` exit 1 even though cut succeeds. The script exits before `[[ -n $guard_line ]] || fail` and prints no `not ok` or explanation. The same applies to mount_line when no bare -t or -- mount exists: it does not simply produce an empty line. In a sandbox substitution of either the merge-base or current quattro boundary file into the new test, exit was 1 with empty stdout and stderr. Capture both pipelines in an `if` and call `fail` on no match or read error, rather than relying on the later `[[ -n ]]` tests.

Related PR #10974 has HTTP 406 for full diff; examined its docs/testing.md file patch through GitHub files API instead. Other open Windows VM PRs mainly add later production-helper and fixture assertions; no claim here that their entire merged suites pass without a combined sandbox run.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The new isolation test exits silently, without its `fail` message, when a listed test lacks the marker gate.

### `grep` misses end the isolation test before `fail`

Under `set -euo pipefail`, a `guard_line=$(grep ... | head -1 | cut ...)` or `mount_line=$(...)` with no match exits the file, so the `fail` naming the file never prints. **Impact:** against the merge-base probe, the test exits 1 with no output.

**Suggested change:** `grep -m1 -nE '...' "$test_file" | cut -d: -f1 || true` in both.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 6d814e1)</summary>

# Reproducer: grep assignments in mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh exit the file silently

Reviewed commit: 6d814e105bdb57f45d2f1944d1617db45f08ca1d (PR #11768 head).

`mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh` runs under `set -euo pipefail` and assigns

```bash
guard_line=$(grep -nE '...' "$test_file" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
mount_line=$(grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*mount (-t|--)' "$test_file" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
```

When `grep` finds no line it exits 1, `pipefail` makes the substitution fail, and `errexit` ends the file at the assignment. So:

1. A mounting test that lost its marker gate makes the file exit 1 with no output. The `fail "$test_name gates its namespace re-exec on a marker variable, not on uid"` line after it never runs.
2. A listed mounting test with no line starting `mount -t` or `mount --` (for example one that mounts only through a sourced helper, or writes `command mount`) also makes the file exit 1 with no output, although its gate is correct. The `if [[ -n $mount_line ]]` check, which is there to let such a test pass, never sees the empty value.

Two test files in the PR's own style show this. Copy them into `test/shell.d/` at the PR head and run each with `bash test/shell.d/<name>`. Neither executes a mount: the first only makes the isolation test grep a uid-gated copy of the probe, and the second lets it run the real boundary probe with the marker set, which refuses before mounting.

## Test 1: `mount-namespace-isolation-diagnostics-test.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh should name the mounting test it rejects.
# This runs it against a scratch copy of the suite whose boundary probe is
# gated on uid again. The isolation test only greps that copy; it never runs it.

set -euo pipefail
source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

make_tree() {
  local tree="$work/$1"
  mkdir -p "$tree/test/shell.d"
  cp "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/base-test.sh" \
    "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh" \
    "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh" \
    "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/windows-vm-compose-test.sh" \
    "$tree/test/shell.d/"
  printf '%s\n' "$tree"
}

# A boundary probe gated on uid again, as before this change. The isolation
# test must fail and say which file lost its marker gate.
tree=$(make_tree uid-gate)
sed -i 's/^if \[\[ \${OMARCHY_WINDOWS_BOUNDARY_NAMESPACE:-0} != 1 \]\]; then$/if ((EUID != 0)); then/' \
  "$tree/test/shell.d/windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh"
grep -q '^if ((EUID != 0)); then$' "$tree/test/shell.d/windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh" ||
  fail "fixture rewrote the boundary guard to a uid gate"
status=0
output=$(bash "$tree/test/shell.d/mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh" 2>&1) || status=$?
(( status != 0 )) || fail "isolation test rejects a uid-gated mounting test" "$output"
[[ $output == *"not ok - windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh gates its namespace re-exec on a marker variable, not on uid"* ]] ||
  fail "isolation test names the uid-gated file when it rejects it" "exit $status, output: [$output]"
pass "isolation test names the uid-gated file when it rejects it"
```

## Test 2: `mount-namespace-isolation-grep-miss-test.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh should accept a marker-gated mounting test
# whose mount lines its grep does not match. This runs it against a scratch
# copy of the suite whose compose test says 'command mount'. The isolation test
# only greps the compose copy; the one file it runs is the real boundary probe,
# with the marker set, which refuses before mounting.

set -euo pipefail
source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

make_tree() {
  local tree="$work/$1"
  mkdir -p "$tree/test/shell.d"
  cp "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/base-test.sh" \
    "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh" \
    "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh" \
    "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/windows-vm-compose-test.sh" \
    "$tree/test/shell.d/"
  printf '%s\n' "$tree"
}

# A marker-gated mounting test with no line starting 'mount -t' or 'mount --'
# (here the compose test written with 'command mount'). The guard is correct,
# so the isolation test should pass.
tree=$(make_tree command-mount)
sed -i 's/^\([[:space:]]*\)mount /\1command mount /' "$tree/test/shell.d/windows-vm-compose-test.sh"
! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*mount (-t|--)' "$tree/test/shell.d/windows-vm-compose-test.sh" ||
  fail "fixture left no direct mount line in the compose test"
status=0
output=$(bash "$tree/test/shell.d/mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh" 2>&1) || status=$?
(( status == 0 )) ||
  fail "isolation test accepts a marker-gated test whose mounts its grep does not match" "exit $status, output: [$output]"
pass "isolation test accepts a marker-gated test whose mounts its grep does not match"
```

### Docs overstate coverage

`docs/testing.md` says it "holds both halves in place for every mounting test", but only the boundary probe gets the fail-closed run and `MOUNTING_TESTS` is a fixed list. **Impact:** authors may assume new mounting tests are checked; three on `quattro` are not.

**Suggested change:** state what the test checks and ask for new mounting tests in `MOUNTING_TESTS`.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Unlisted mounting tests on `quattro` 8b4eae6:**
- `remove-dev-env-sudo-security-test.sh`: top-level `mount -t tmpfs` and `mount --bind`, gated on `${OMARCHY_REMOVE_DEV_ENV_SECURITY_NS:-0} != "1"`. The quoted `"1"` does not match the isolation test's guard pattern, so listing it as-is ends the isolation test silently (the `grep` issue above); with the suggested change it fails with the "not on uid" message, although the file does gate on a marker.
- `update-stay-awake-security-test.sh` and `security-fingerprint-remove-test.sh`: mount only inside `unshare` children (`bash -c` or a heredoc), a pattern the convention text does not describe.

**Rebase:** the PR conflicts with `quattro` on the probe's skip line (`quattro` commit 599a6a66 changed `pass` to `skip`). Keeping `skip` with the PR's new message lets the runner list the skip; on a merge resolved that way the isolation test passes and the probe prints `# SKIP` when no namespace is available.

**Optional test improvement:** the ordering check compares the first `mount` line with the guard's opening `if`, so a mount inserted inside the guard block, before `exec unshare`, still passes all four checks. Comparing against the block's `exec ... unshare` line or closing `fi` would catch it (not tested). Reproducer in the next block.


**Optional hardening:** the fail-closed check passes when the inner `readlink /proc/self/ns/mnt` fails, because an empty string differs from the recorded value. Harm needs a lapsed re-exec as well, so this is unlikely. Reading it once with `current_mount_ns=$(readlink /proc/self/ns/mnt) || current_mount_ns=`, then requiring `-n $current_mount_ns` and comparing `$current_mount_ns`, made both failing-read cases refuse in a sandbox run.

**Verified** (sandbox, uid 0 inside a throwaway user namespace, stub-logged `mount`):
- Merge base: all four tmpfs mounts (`/run`, `/var`, `/home`, `/home/alice`) land in the caller's namespace and remain after the file exits. Head: all four happen in a different namespace and none remain.
- Root without `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`: head skips; merge base failed with `mount: /run: permission denied.`.
- The fail-closed check refuses before any mount when the recorded namespace equals the current one or was never recorded.
- The new file is picked up by `test/shell`'s `*-test.sh` glob and passes at the head and on the head merged with `quattro`.

**Related PR:** #9834 ("Refuse to run the shell suite as root") addresses the same root-runner hazard (suite refusal plus a root skip in the compose test) and merges cleanly with this PR.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: ordering gap (fails at 6d814e1)</summary>

# Reproducer (test-validity note): the ordering check does not see a mount placed before the re-exec

Reviewed commit: 6d814e105bdb57f45d2f1944d1617db45f08ca1d (PR #11768 head).

For each listed test, `mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh` checks only that the first line matching `^[[:space:]]*mount (-t|--)` comes after the first `if [[ ${OMARCHY_...:-0} != 1 ]]; then` line, then passes "enters its namespace before mounting anything". A mount inside that `if` block, before the `exec unshare`, is after the guard line, so it passes, yet it would run in the caller's namespace. The behavioural probe does not cover it either, because it starts the boundary probe with the marker already set and so skips the block. The probe's own runtime check sits after the block and does not cover it.

Copy this file into `test/shell.d/` at the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/early-mount-ordering-test.sh`. It never executes the mutated block: the isolation test only greps it.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh reports "enters its namespace before
# mounting anything". A mount placed inside the marker guard, before the
# unshare re-exec, still runs in the caller's namespace. Check whether the
# isolation test notices. Nothing here executes the mutated guard block: the
# isolation test only greps it, and runs the probe with the marker already set.

set -euo pipefail
source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

tree="$work/early-mount"
mkdir -p "$tree/test/shell.d"
cp "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/base-test.sh" \
  "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh" \
  "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh" \
  "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/windows-vm-compose-test.sh" \
  "$tree/test/shell.d/"

probe="$tree/test/shell.d/windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh"
sed -i '/^if \[\[ \${OMARCHY_WINDOWS_BOUNDARY_NAMESPACE:-0} != 1 \]\]; then$/a\  mount -t tmpfs -o size=1m early-mount /run' "$probe"
grep -q '^  mount -t tmpfs -o size=1m early-mount /run$' "$probe" || fail "fixture inserted the early mount"

status=0
output=$(bash "$tree/test/shell.d/mount-namespace-isolation-test.sh" 2>&1) || status=$?
(( status != 0 )) || fail "isolation test rejects a mount placed before the namespace re-exec" "$output"
pass "isolation test rejects a mount placed before the namespace re-exec"
```

## Actual output at the PR head

A tighter check (not tested here) would compare the first mount line against the guard block's closing `fi` or its `exec ... unshare` line rather than its opening `if`.
